segments.he: כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְיָאֵשׁ מִן הַצְּעָקָה אֲזַי הַצַּדִּיק מוֹדִיעַ לוֹ כִּי
segments.en: This is the aspect of hisbodidus and conversation — this is prayer — which every person must pour out his speech before Hashem every single day, to request for his soul from Hashem that He grant him merit to draw close to His service in truth. And this is the foundation of everything — all one's service and one's being a Jew depends on this, as we have explained many times. And more than what is written there, we heard from his holy mouth directly many many times — many awesome conversations on this matter that are impossible to fully explain in writing. And he said that all the Tzaddikim and the upright ones merited to come to what they came to only through this — through conversation between oneself and one's Maker in the vernacular in which they speak, as explained in the printed books.

segments.he: כְּשֶׁאָדָם נִתְרַחֵק מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ חַס וְשָׁלוֹם מִכָּל שֶׁכֵּן כְּשֶׁנּוֹפֵל לְתַאֲוֹת רָעוֹת וַעֲבֵרוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. אֲזַי הוּא בְּחִינַת רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל בָּנֶיהָ וְכוּ'.
segments.en: At first glance this is difficult — for our Rabbis of blessed memory taught: everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven. And if so, how is prayer relevant here, since Hashem has entrusted free choice to us? Even so, in truth we find that all the Tzaddikim engaged in this — requesting from Hashem to save them from the evil inclination and draw them close to His service. As we heard with full mouths from the true Tzaddikim who were near our time. And also in the words of our Rabbis of blessed memory in the Talmud and other books we find many prayers that they recited each day to be saved from the evil inclination. And also from the fixed prayers established for us each day by the Men of the Great Assembly we see this — for we pray three times every day: "Return us, our Father, to Your Torah and bring us close, our King, to Your service, and return us in complete repentance before You." It emerges that we pray to Hashem three times every day to merit repentance and to serve Him — even though this depends on human free choice. And similarly many other fixed prayers, all founded on this petition — to merit the service of Hashem. And the entire Book of Tehillim is founded upon these prayers and supplications to merit drawing close to Him. And in truth it is impossible to understand this — for it is among the questions that cannot be resolved in any way except through faith alone.

segments.he: כִּי הַשְּׁכִינָה שֶׁהִוא קְדֻשַּׁת יִשְׂרָאֵל נִקְרֵאת רָחֵל כַּיָּדוּעַ וַאֲזַי הִיא בִּבְחִינַת כְּרָחֵל לִפְנֵי גזְזֶיהָ נֶאֶלָמָה דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁקְּדֻשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל הִיא בֵּין הַקְּלִפּוֹת וְסִטְרִין אָחֳרָנִין הַמְּעִיקִין וּמְצֵרִין לָהּ. וּמִגּדֶל חֲלִישׁוּתָהּ עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי עֲוֹנוֹתָיו הִיא כְּרָחֵל לִפְנֵי גזְזֶיהָ נֶאֶלָמָה שֶׁהֵן גּוֹזְזִין וְגוֹזְלִין אוֹתָהּ וְנוֹטְלִין מִמֶּנָּה הוֹדָהּ וְתִפְאַרְתָּהּ וְהִיא נֶאֶלָמָה בֵּינֵיהֶם. וַאֲזַי הִיא בְּחִינַת שְׁכִינָה מָה אוֹמֶרֶת קַלַּנִי מֵראשִׁי קַלַּנִי מִזְּרוֹעִי וְכוּ' כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה. וּכְשֶׁזֶּה הָרָחוֹק מְאד נִתְעוֹרֵר בְּעצֶם רִחוּקוֹ וְאֵינוֹ מְיָאֵשׁ עַצְמוֹ בְּשׁוּם אפֶן וּבוֹכֶה וְצוֹעֵק לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד זֶה בְּחִינַת קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע נְהִי בְּכִי תַמְרוּרִים רָחֵל מְבַכָּה עַל בָּנֶיהָ מֵאֲנָה לְהִנָּחֵם עַל בָּנֶיהָ בְּגִין כִּי אֵינֶנּוּ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ) הַיְנוּ שֶׁקְּדֻשַּׁת הַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת רָחֵל הִיא בּוֹכָה וּמְבַכָּה עַל בָּנֶיהָ הַיְנוּ עַל מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים שֶׁלָּהּ שֶׁאִבְּדָה עַל יְדֵי תַּאֲוֹתֶיהָ הָרָעוֹת כִּי הַמַּעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים נִקְרָאִים בָּנִים כִּי עִקַּר תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים. וְהִיא בּוֹכָה בִּמְרִירוּת גָּדוֹל מְאד בִּבְחִינַת נְהִי בְּכִי תַמְרוּרִים עַד אֲשֶׁר קוֹל בְּרָמָה נִשְׁמָע כְּתַרְגּוּמוֹ קַל בְּרוּם שְׁמַיָּא אִשְׁתְּמַע וְכוּ' וּמִגּדֶל כְּאֵבָהּ שֶׁהִיא רוֹאָה שֶׁזֶּה זְמַן רַב אֲשֶׁר עֲדַיִן לא עָלְתָה אֲרוּכָה לְמַכָּתָהּ וְהִיא צוֹעֶקֶת וּבוֹכָה זֶה זְמַן זְמַנִּים טוּבָא וַעֲדַיִן הִיא רְחוֹקָה מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּל כָּךְ. וְעַל כֵּן מֵאֲנָה לְהִנָּחֵם עַל בָּנֶיהָ כִּי אֵינֶנּוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּהַר בְּגִין כִּי אֵינֶנּוּ. הַיְנוּ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת בְּלִבָּהּ אֵיךְ אֶפְשָׁר לְנַחֲמֵנוּ וַאֲנִי יוֹדֵעַ כִּי אֵינֶנּוּ.
segments.en: And when Rabbainu of blessed memory informed me of the matter of hisbodidus and conversation between oneself and one's Maker, I spoke with him a little about this — but is not man a free agent? He did not answer me explicitly, only dismissively — as if to say: even so. Meaning: even though this is difficult and the matter cannot be clarified for you and resolved, even so one must conduct oneself thus. And I could not ask further — for I knew that this question can be raised against all the prayers our Sages of blessed memory established for us long ago regarding repentance and drawing close to Hashem — such as the blessing of "Return us" and others. Therefore one must rely only on faith — to believe in our Sages of blessed memory that all of them walked in this path and led us in this path to multiply prayer and supplication to Hashem, to merit the service of Hashem. For this is the primary foundation that everything depends upon.

segments.he: כִּי אֵין ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמִּי עֲדַיִן כִּי אֲנִי רָחוֹק מֵה' יִתְבָּרַךְ מְאד מְאד.
segments.en: Therefore one must specifically multiply prayers and supplications and conversations between oneself and one's Maker — cries and pleas and appeasements and implorations to Hashem to grant one merit to draw close to His service. And this is the primary prayer — for: "for this let every devout one pray to You at a time of finding" [Tehillim 32:6] — "only that floods of great water not reach him" — lest the floods of great water overwhelm him, which are the insolent waters, the evil desires of this world that flood at all times, and have already overwhelmed very many people, Heaven have mercy. May the Omnipresent have mercy upon us and upon all Yisrael and save us from them. And there is no wisdom and no understanding and no counsel to stand against them except through prayer and supplication to Hashem to be saved from them. For even though a person has free choice, even so the primary thing is prayer and supplication to Hashem about this. For through one's choice — choosing the good path and turning from the evil path — one subdues the kelipas that come from the breaking of the vessels and refines the good from them. For free choice is in the intellect — which has the power to choose good and reject evil. And human intellect has power only to subdue and nullify the kelipas that come from the breaking of the vessels — which contain many holy sparks, all refined through wisdom. But there are confusions and other sides and obstacles to holiness that come from the aspect of the vacant space — where there is no intellect or wisdom, only faith alone, which is the aspect of prayer and supplication and cries and pleas to Hashem to save one from them. For about this it is said: "Every day a person's inclination overpowers him, and were it not for the Holy One blessed be He who helps him, he would fall into its hand" — for from this evil inclination drawn from the vacant space it is impossible to be saved in any way except through Heavenly assistance. Therefore one must pray very, very greatly and beseech to be saved from it — for there, intellect is of no help; on the contrary, through intellect and wisdom one sinks there, Heaven forbid. Only the primary thing is faith — which is the aspect of prayer. And in truth this is the primary free choice — that one overrides one's own reasoning entirely and relies on faith alone, and multiplies prayer and supplication. For the adversary distorts a person's heart so much that even this is hard for the person — even though in truth it is a very simple matter. Even so, he confuses and distorts one's mind so much that most of the time this very matter of prayer and hisbodidus is harder for a person than all other difficult labors — and all this is because of a lack of complete faith, which is the primary foundation.

segments.he: אֲבָל אַף עַל פִּי כֵן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא רְחוֹקָה כָּל כָּךְ מֵאַחַר שֶׁמְּחַזֶּקֶת עַצְמָהּ עֲדַיִן לִצְעק וְלִבְכּוֹת לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ תָּמִיד. אֲזַי נִתְעוֹרְרִין רַחֲמֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמֵאִיר עָלֶיהָ הֶאָרָה וְהִתְחַזְּקוּת מִלְּמַעְלָה בִּבְחִינַת כּה אָמַר ה' מִנְעִי קוֹלֵךְ מִבֶּכִי וְעֵינַיִךְ מִדִּמְעָה כִּי יֵשׁ שָׂכָר לִפְעֻלָּתֵךְ וְיֵשׁ תִּקְוָה לְאַחֲרִיתֵךְ וְכוּ' וְכָל זֶה עַל יְדֵי הַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר הַגָּדוֹל בְּמַעֲלָה מְאד שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יִשָּׂשְׂכָר שֶׁמֵּאִיר בְּכָל נֶפֶשׁ וְנֶפֶשׁ וּמוֹדִיעַ לָהּ כִּי עֲדַיִן יֵשׁ שָׂכָר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה כִּי אֵין שׁוּם יֵאוּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם כִּי אֵין שׁוּם דִּבּוּר וְלא שׁוּם צְעָקָה נֶאֱבֶדֶת אֲפִלּוּ צְעָקָה מִשְּׁאוֹל תַּחְתִּיּוֹת אֵינָהּ נֶאֱבֶדֶת לְעוֹלָם (כַּמְבאָר בִּדְבָרֵינוּ כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים): (הִלְכוֹת פֶּסַח הֲלָכָה ט אוֹת יב):
segments.en: And therefore one who merits to accustom oneself in this and to multiply prayers and conversations to Hashem to grant one merit to draw close to His service — in this itself one is a free agent in having chosen to live in the true path of faith and prayer, as it is written: "I have chosen the path of faith" [Tehillim 119:30]. For in truth this is the primary free choice — that one sets aside one's reasoning and chooses faith and prayer, which is the primary foundation upon which all the Torah stands. As it is written: "Havakkuk came and established them all on one — and the righteous person shall live by his faith" [Makkos 24a]. And then when one has complete faith and multiplies prayers and conversations to Hashem to grant one merit to return to Him in truth — then Hashem helps one to merit serving Him in Torah and commandments, and illuminates one's eyes in His Torah until one merits to understand Torah and service as much as is possible for human intellect. And through these two aspects — faith and the holy intellect that flows from faith — one subdues the two kinds of kelipas described above, drawn from the aspect of the vacant space and from the aspect of the breaking of vessels. For both together are good — to draw close to Him. And about this it is said: "two are better than one" [Koheles 4:9] — "for if they fall, the one will raise his companion." For Torah and prayer — which are the aspects of intellect and faith — are interdependent, and one strengthens and establishes the other. But the primary is faith.
